The animals are messengers of the gods, and they will bestow their blessing on whoever raises the most magnificent altar. Over ten rounds you take pedestal cubes from the five supply spaces of the shared board and stack them on your own cloud-covered altar, growing it upward and outward. When a pillar meets the requirements of a totem, that totem comes to roost on top of it and starts scoring for you, and each totem - bird, wolf, horse, cat and dragon - scores in a completely different way. Altar cards give every player private goals and a unique starting altar, and only four of the five totems are in play each game, so no two altars ever rise the same way. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal 2 Setup 3 On Your Turn 3.1 Build pedestals 3.2 Build a totem 4 Placement Rules 5 Revealing Altar Cards 6 End of Round 7 The Last Totem 8 Scoring 9 The Five Totems 10 Game Options 11 Glossary Goal Over 10 rounds you grow your own altar in the clouds: you place cloud tiles , stack pedestal cubes on them, and raise totems on top of the columns. Pedestals, totems and revealed altar cards all score at the end. The highest score wins. Each player builds their own altar. You never build on another player's altar; what you compete for is the shared supply of pedestals. Setup 1. The number of pedestal slots on the main board depends on the player count: 3 slots with 2 players, 4 with 3 players, 5 with 4 players. Unused slots are blocked. 2. Four of the five totems are used in a game (see Game options below). The two altar cards that refer to the unused totem are removed from the deck. 3. Each player receives one 2×2 starting cloud tile and three altar cards . You choose one card to reveal — that card defines your starting altar — and the other two stay face down as your secret goals . All players choose at the same time, so you cannot react to anyone else's choice. 4. Build your starting altar exactly as printed on the card you revealed, taking those pedestals from the bag. If the card shows a cloud icon, also gain and place one extra cloud tile. 5. The start player puts 2 pedestals from the bag into every pedestal slot . Nobody looks inside the bag. On Your Turn You take exactly one of these two actions: 1. Build pedestals 2. Build a totem In addition, you may reveal altar cards at any time during your turn, as often as you like . Revealing does not use up your action. Build pedestals 1. Choose one pedestal slot and take all the pedestals in it. If no slot has any pedestals left, draw 2 pedestals at random from the bag instead. 2. Take the pedestals one at a time and either place it on your altar or return it to the bag . 3. For each pedestal you returned to the bag, gain one cloud tile and place it. Build a totem 1. Choose a totem whose placement condition is met and place it on your altar. 2. Immediately take that totem's blessing . 3. The totem scores at the end of the game. Each kind of totem can be built more than once during a game, as long as its condition is met. Placement Rules Pedestals • A pedestal can only be placed on your own cloud tiles . You cannot place one where you have no cloud tile. • You may stack, but a pedestal may only be stacked on a column whose bottom pedestal is of the same kind . • Exception: a pedestal of the same kind as one sitting in the dragon's hoard may be stacked on any column, whatever that column is made of. Cloud tiles • A new cloud tile must be placed edge-adjacent to one of your existing cloud tiles. Touching only at a corner, or placing it apart from your altar, is not allowed.
